shifts.summary: The shift was reported overall as Moderate, with reports differing between Difficult and Easy to Moderate. Reasoning was seen as ranging from Easy to Moderate, with many statement‑wise questions and some candidates stuck. General Awareness difficulty varied, most reports calling it Difficult, covering extensive current‑affairs and constitutional topics. Quantitative ability was described from Moderate to Difficult, featuring formula‑heavy and advanced problems. English was generally Easy to Moderate, though advanced vocabulary challenged some candidates.

intro: On 22 October 2026, Shift 1 of the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam was reported as Moderate overall, though individual reports varied between Difficult and Easy to Moderate. Reasoning difficulty ranged from Easy to Moderate, while General Awareness was largely described as Difficult, covering extensive current‑affairs and constitutional topics. Quantitative Ability was seen as Moderate to Difficult with formula‑heavy problems, and English was generally Easy to Moderate but included some advanced vocabulary. Figures such as the 75–85 % good‑attempt range are unofficial, and SSC normalises scores across shifts. Shifts 2 and 3 remain pending, with no usable analysis published yet.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty reported for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 22 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 was reported as Moderate overall, though some sources described it as Difficult while others said Easy to Moderate. No official overall rating has been released for Shifts 2 and 3.

faqs.q: How did the Reasoning section perform on 22 October 2026?
faqs.a: For Shift 1, Reasoning difficulty was described as ranging from Easy to Moderate, with many statement‑wise questions and some candidates experiencing difficulty. No analysis is yet available for Shifts 2 and 3.

faqs.q: What was the difficulty level of General Awareness on 22 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 reports indicate General Awareness was largely Difficult, covering extensive current‑affairs and constitutional topics. No usable analysis has been published for Shifts 2 and 3.

faqs.q: What information is currently available for Shifts 2 and 3 of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 22 October 2026?
faqs.a: Both Shift 2 and Shift 3 are still pending; no usable analysis has been published for them yet, and a review will be added when sufficient candidate evidence is gathered.

faqs.q: Are the reported good‑attempt figures for 22 October 2026 reliable?
faqs.a: The good‑attempt range of 75–85 % for Shift 1 is unofficial and should be treated as indicative only; SSC normalises scores across shifts, and the figure is not confirmed as an official statistic.
